references.name: Lunar south polar highlands (pole-centred region containing Artemis III candidate regions)
references.illumination_summary: Peaks along the rim of Shackleton are illuminated about 80–90% of each lunar orbit (literature); PSRs never illuminated
references.ice_evidence: Cold traps >80° latitude host most water-ice cold-trap area (Hayne et al. 2021 summarised in wiki:Lunar water).
references.hazards: steep crater walls and massif slopes; long low-angle shadows; extreme thermal gradients between sunlit and shadowed terrain; no atmosphere; radiation; 1/6 g
references.mission_objectives: crewed landing (Artemis III candidate regions); polar volatiles prospecting; sample of ancient crust; power from near-continuous illumination

references.name: Shackleton crater and rim vicinity
references.illumination_summary: rim peaks ~80–90% illuminated; interior in perpetual darkness
references.ice_evidence: LOLA reflectance analysis suggests up to 22% of Shackleton's surface may be covered in ice (wiki:Lunar water; Zuber et al. 2012).
references.hazards: ~4.2 km deep conical crater with steep walls; permanent shadow in interior; thermal extremes
references.mission_objectives: PSR volatiles access; illuminated rim for power; ancient crust sampling

references.name: Malapert massif
references.illumination_summary: two ridge regions illuminated ~74% of the lunar year (Bussey et al. 2010 as cited by Allender et al. 2019)
references.ice_evidence: Small-scale PSRs in surrounding area (Allender et al. 2019).
references.hazards: massif rises ~5 km; slopes 15–25° on ridge approaches (Allender et al. 2019)
references.mission_objectives: Artemis III candidate region; Earth line-of-sight communications; SPA basin rim material

references.name: Cabeus crater permanently shadowed region (LCROSS impact target)
references.illumination_summary: main crater lit ~25% of lunar day; western part in permanent shadow
references.ice_evidence: LCROSS ejecta water concentration 5.6 ± 2.9% by mass (Colaprete et al. 2010, as reported in wiki:Lunar water).
references.hazards: permanent darkness; <100 K surfaces; crater walls

references.name: Marius Hills pit (mare volcanic dome field)
references.dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
references.illumination_summary: pit floor partly overhung (LROC Pits Atlas: Overhang=Y)
references.hazards: ~40 m deep pit (LROC atlas); boulder-covered floor; overhangs
references.mission_objectives: lava-tube / subsurface habitat scouting; radiation and thermal shelter

references.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
references.dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
references.illumination_summary: pit floor partly in permanent shadow beneath overhang
references.hazards: ~100 m deep pit (NASA 2022 release); vertical walls; illuminated floor >420 K peak (modeled)
references.mission_objectives: lava-tube / subsurface habitat scouting; thermal-stable shelter

references.name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base (mare regolith plains)
references.dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
references.illumination_summary: equatorial day/night cycle (~29.5 Earth days synodic)
references.hazards: regolith dust; small craters and boulders
references.mission_objectives: mare regolith handling; surface mobility on plains

references.name: Jezero crater delta (Perseverance landing site)
references.dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
references.mission_objectives: astrobiology/biosignatures in lacustrine sediments; sample caching for return
